prompt.context: Our client is a healthcare provider for animals. The client has recently developed a product that enables cows to increase milk production by 20%. They have turned to you to figure out how to price this new product in order to maximize profits.
prompt.question: How should the client price this new product in order to maximize profits?

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have a patent for this product?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company does not have a patent for the product.

clarifying_info.q: In which geography is the company operating?
clarifying_info.a: The company is operating in the US.

clarifying_info.q: How is the product sold and administered?
clarifying_info.a: The product is sold and administered in doses.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a competitor in this space?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, there is one competitor with a similar product that is as safe as our client's but only increases milk production by 5%. The competitor prices its product at $300 per dose. Cows need to be administered 2 doses per week regardless of which product is used.

clarifying_info.q: What are the costs to the client?
clarifying_info.a: Total cost to the client is $30 per dose, leveraging existing knowledge and operations for fixed and variable costs.

framework: Pricing Strategies: Evaluate cost-based pricing vs. price-based costing
Competitive Analysis: Benchmark against competitor product price and differentiation (5% vs. 20% milk production increase)
Revenues: Price per dose x number of doses per cow per year x number of cows (market sizing)
Costs: Fixed costs (equipment, plant) and variable costs (raw materials, distribution, production labor, marketing & sales) — total $30 per dose
Profits: Revenue minus total costs; assess margin and profit potential

questions.prompt: How would you calculate the potential profit opportunity for this product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure: Revenue = price/dose x doses/cow/year x number of cows. Requires market sizing for US dairy cows and a reasonable market share assumption. Candidate should note our product is 4x more efficient than the competitor's, justifying high market share. Cost = $30/dose x same volume. Profit = Revenue - Cost. Strong candidates will reason through the competitive price anchor of $300 and why matching it is rational given price sensitivity.

math.setup: Revenue = price/dose x doses/year x cows captured. Cost = cost/dose x doses/year x cows captured. Market share assumed high given 4x efficiency advantage.
steps: Assume 20% market share (reasonable given 4x efficiency): 10M x 20% = 2M cows
Doses per year: 2 doses/week x 52 weeks = 104 doses (round to 100)
Revenue at $300/dose: $300 x 100 x 2,000,000 = $60B (or $62.4B using 104 doses)
math.answer: ~$54B annual profit potential at a price of $300/dose with a 90% margin

brainstorming.prompt: What additional company capabilities would be needed to successfully launch and capture market share for this product?

categories.name: Sales & Marketing
ideas: Build sales force to reach dairy farmers
Develop marketing materials highlighting 4x efficiency advantage over competitor
Invest in farmer education and product demonstrations

categories.name: Patent & Legal
ideas: Begin patent registration process immediately to protect the product
Monitor for competitor replication given no current patent protection

categories.name: Post-Sale Support
ideas: Establish customer support for ongoing product administration guidance
Create maintenance and follow-up programs to ensure proper dosing

categories.name: R&D
ideas: Continue R&D investment using high margins to maintain innovation lead
Develop next-generation products to stay ahead of competitors

recommendation: Price the product at $300 per dose — matching the competitor's price while offering a 4x superior product (20% vs. 5% milk production increase)
At $300/dose with $30/dose costs, the client achieves a 90% margin; high margins allow room for promotions if needed to accelerate adoption
Customers are price sensitive, so pricing at parity with the competitor is appropriate even though the product is significantly better — farmers will switch for the same price and better results
risks: No patent protection means the product could be replicated by competitors
Threat of new entrants developing even more efficient products over time
Competitor may lower its price in response, compressing margins
next_steps: Analyze potential competitive response to the launch
Start the patent registration process immediately
Launch the new product with sales and marketing support
Continue R&D investment in parallel to maintain innovation advantage and defend against future competition
